newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to allow resident Chinese reporters.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to allow resident Chinese reporters.

text.p: Taiwan will soon start accepting applications from Chinese journalists to report from the island for periods as long as two years, an official at the cabinet's Mainland Affairs Council said on Monday.

The top policymaking body for China approved the draft at a board meeting, allowing Chinese journalists to work in Taiwan for up to one year, with the possibility of another year's extension, the official said.
"The draft will go into effect after the premier's final approval, which will take about two weeks," the official said by telephone.
"We welcome their applications," he added. Only a handful of Chinese reporters have visited Taiwan since a political thaw that began in the late 1980s.
Chinese reporters should apply to the cabinet's Government Information Office with their news coverage proposals, and their spouses can also apply to live in Taiwan, he said.
Taiwan, political rival of China since a civil war separated them in 1949, allows mainland Chinese to live on the island on a case-by-case basis.
Both governments in Taipei and Beijing say they want reunification, but under very different terms.
